title: Data Processing and Image Registration
author: Elizabeth Neumann
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bt8jnrun
materials: Save the transformed and registered post-AF image.

steps.title: Convert Bruker raw files
steps.instruction: Convert each Bruker (.d) raw file into a custom binary data format in profile mode at the instrument's native spectral resolution.

steps.title: Mass alignment and calibration
steps.instruction: Align and calibrate the dataset using the Python msalign package (https://github.com/lukasz-migas/msalign). Estimate spectral mis‑alignment per pixel and correct it with PCHIP interpolation or a linear shift. First align spectra based on automatically selected peaks, then recalibrate using at least three well‑characterized lipids:

steps.title: Create mean mass spectrum
steps.instruction: Generate a mean mass spectrum by averaging the intensity of each mass bin across all pixels in the aligned and calibrated dataset.

steps.title: Peak picking and LIPIDMAPS annotation
steps.instruction: Perform peak picking on the mean spectrum and annotate each m/z value using the LIPIDMAPS database with the following search criteria:

steps.title: Calculate ppm errors and filter
steps.instruction: Calculate the ppm error for each assignment; discard any assignment with an error > 5 ppm (most assignments are < 3 ppm). Also calculate ppm error for common lipids [PC(32:0)+H]+ and [PC(34:1)+H]+; if the error exceeds 3 ppm, re‑calibrate the entire dataset using additional well‑characterized ions.

steps.title: Optional LC‑MS/MS annotation
steps.instruction: If LC‑MS/MS data are available, annotate each m/z value against the LC‑MS/MS list; otherwise proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Extract ion images
steps.instruction: Extract peak intensities from the calibrated dataset using one of the following options:

substeps.instruction: 1. Use an untargeted feature list that has not been narrowed down previously.
2. Use the identified feature list generated in the previous step.
In either case, create narrow 3‑5 m/z extraction windows for each selected peak; the window width must be kept small to avoid mixing poorly resolved ions.

steps.title: TIC‑based normalization
steps.instruction: Compute total ion current (TIC)‑based normalization factors for each pixel after alignment and calibration.

steps.title: Export intensities to CSV
steps.instruction: Export the extracted peak intensities to a columnar CSV file. Concatenate the x‑ and y‑coordinates from the registration step with the selected ions in the format: x, y, m/z₁, m/z₂, …, m/z_N.

steps.title: Convert CSV to imzML
steps.instruction: Read the CSV table into Python and export the peak intensities to an imzML file using the pyimzML library (https://github.com/lukasz-migas/pyimzML).

steps.title: Generate IMS pixel map
steps.instruction: Create a MALDI imaging mass‑spectrometry pixel map using regToolboxMSRC (https://github.com/nhpatterson/regtoolboxmsrc).

steps.title: Select laser marks in FIJI
steps.instruction: In FIJI/ImageJ (https://fiji.sc), select the laser‑ablation marks in the post‑acquisition autofluorescence (post‑AF) image and the corresponding IMS pixels in the IMS pixel map.

steps.title: Compute affine transformation
steps.instruction: Run the “Landmark Correspondences” FIJI plugin to compute an affine transformation: set the post‑AF image as the source and the IMS pixel map as the template, then resample the post‑AF image to the IMS grid.

steps.title: Register other microscopy modalities
steps.instruction: Use wsireg (https://github.com/nhpatterson/wsireg) to align additional microscopy images (e.g., CODEX multiplexed IF, pre‑IMS AF, PAS) to the saved post‑AF image. wsireg will generate pyramidal OME‑TIFF files for each registered image.

steps.title: Finalize image overlay
steps.instruction: Confirm that all images are sampled in the same coordinate system as the IMS pixel map; overlay the IMS data onto microscopy images by scaling the IMS data to match the microscopy resolution.
